en.headline: Employer groups urge freeze on domestic helper minimum wage
en.dek: Two employer organisations petitioned the government on Saturday, citing a survey in which most respondents said they could not afford a rise and might dismiss helpers if wages increased.
body: A coalition of Hong Kong employers of foreign domestic helpers called on the government to freeze the minimum allowable wage and food allowance for this year, warning that any increase could lead to widespread dismissals.

The International Domestic Service Industry Development Federation and the Quadripartite Alliance for Harmonious Employment Practices, together with about 30 employer representatives, submitted a petition on Saturday. They cited a July survey of more than 6,200 employers in which over 97 per cent hoped for a freeze and 84 per cent said they might not be able to afford a pay rise.

A federation spokeswoman said many employers themselves were unemployed or facing pay cuts. The groups also proposed a pay-for-performance mechanism that would allow higher rewards for stronger performers. The government regularly reviews the minimum wage with reference to economic conditions and stakeholder views.

zh.headline: 外傭僱主團體促凍結最低工資 稱加薪或致大量解僱
zh.dek: 兩個僱主團體周六向政府請願，指調查顯示逾九成僱主希望凍薪，八成半表示難以負擔加薪或考慮解僱外傭。
body: 國際家政服務業持續發展聯會及國際政商勞資事務和諧關愛會周六聯同約30名僱主代表向政府請願，促請凍結2026年外籍家庭傭工規定最低工資及膳食津貼。
團體引用7月對逾6,200名僱主的調查，指超過97%希望凍結或下調，84%表示若加薪將超出負擔能力，可能考慮解僱外傭。發言人指不少僱主自身面對失業或減薪。
團體同時建議設立按表現調整薪酬的機制。政府定期按經濟及勞工市場情況、僱主負擔能力及持份者意見檢討外傭最低許可工資水平。
